newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese university teachers on one-day strike.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese university teachers on one-day strike.

text.p: Some 1,600 lecturers at state-run Lebanese University staged a one-day strike on Friday to protest against the government's refusal to meet their long-standing demands.

The taecher's demands include the allocation of 150 billion Lebanese pounds ($97 million) for the university in the state budget, full tenure for contract staff, a new pay scale, a cost of living pay rise and other pay benefits.

Parliament will end on Saturday a four-day debate of the draft 1997 state budget which proposes revenues of 4,100 billion pounds and expenditures of 6,433 billion pounds -- a deficit of about 36 percent. The budget allocates 124 billion for the Lebanese University.
The strike which closed down the university's campuses across Lebanon, idled 45,000 students.

"It is a general strike that closed all university campuses in Beirut and the regions and students are now discussing with their teachers and administrators reasons for the strike," professor Issam Khalifeh, head of the executive committee of the university teachers told Reuters.
"A one-day strike is the first step towards a tougher action and more comprehensive steps if the government policies remain unchanged with regard to the university needs and demands," he added.
